record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Do there exist inner functions in any strictly pseudo-convex domain of Cn , n ≥ 2? Alexandrov (no citation) and independently Løw (no citation) and Hakim and Sibony [361] have shown the existence of inner functions in the case of the ball. (R. Zeinstra)

evidence.quote: Do there exist inner functions in any strictly pseudo-convex domain of Cn , n ≥ 2?
There is a positive answer by Løw (see [531] and [532]) if the domain is smoothly bounded.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a strictly pseudoconvex domain (i.e., a bounded domain admitting a $C^2$ defining function $\rho$ such that $\Omega = \{\rho < 0\}$, $d\rho \neq 0$ on $\partial\Omega$, and the Levi form of $\rho$ is positive definite at every boundary point). A bounded holomorphic function $f \in H^\infty(\Omega)$ is called an inner function if its boundary values $f^*$, which exist almost everywhere on $\partial\Omega$ with respect to surface measure, satisfy $|f^*(z)| = 1$ for almost every $z \in \partial\Omega$. A nonconstant inner function is called nontrivial.

Question: For every strictly pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ with $n \geq 2$, does there exist a nontrivial inner function on $\Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: For the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$, the existence of nontrivial inner functions was established independently by Aleksandrov and by Hakim–Sibony / Løw around 1981–1982. Løw (Math. Z. 185 (1984), 191–210) extended this to all smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$, giving a positive answer to the problem in the standard $C^\infty$-smooth setting.

status_evidence.title: Inner functions and boundary values in H∞(Ω) and A(Ω) in smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domains
status_evidence.snippet: Løw, Math. Z. 185 (1984), 191–210, constructs inner functions on smoothly bounded strictly (and more general) pseudoconvex domains in C^n.
status_evidence.claim: Inner functions exist on all smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains in C^n, n≥2.

status_evidence.title: Complete proper holomorphic embeddings of strictly pseudoconvex domains (Drinovec lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Aleksandrov, Hakim, Sibony, and Løw proved the existence of nonconstant bounded holomorphic functions on B^n with unimodular boundary values; Løw's method extends to strictly pseudoconvex domains with C^2 boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of inner functions on strictly pseudoconvex domains with C^2 boundary follows from the Hakim–Sibony–Løw method.
